experiments.name: Kepler's Laws of Orbital Motion
experiments.objective: Analyzed Cartesian trajectory data of two planets to computationally rediscover Kepler’s laws. Calculated angular momentum and verified its conservation, identified the perihelion direction, and performed a coordinate transformation aligning the orbital plane (angular momentum along the z-axis and perihelion along the x-axis). Demonstrated planar motion by reducing the system to two dimensions and analyzed orbital characteristics using Python.

experiments.name: The Brachistochrone Problem
experiments.objective: Investigated the problem of determining the curve of fastest descent between two points under gravity. Derived the analytical solution using the Euler–Lagrange equation, obtaining the cycloidal trajectory. Independently implemented a numerical optimization approach using a trial-and-error (evolutionary) algorithm, where candidate paths were iteratively modified and evaluated via a time functional. Verified convergence to the cycloid by comparing numerical and analytical solutions through Python-based simulations and plots.

experiments.name: The Hanging Chain Problem
experiments.objective: Investigated the equilibrium shape of a hanging chain suspended between two supports at equal height. Experimentally measured the maximum sag as a function of the distance between supports and compared it with theoretical predictions. Derived the catenary curve using calculus of variations by minimizing gravitational potential energy, and validated the model by overlaying experimental and analytical results using Python-based plotting.
